newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent faces $19-$19.10 test again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent faces $19-$19.10 test again.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ IPE Brent faces a test at $19 a barrel again and Friday's failure to close above that, combined with the fact that stochastics are overbought, point to short term weakness.
+ But longer term trendlines suggest prices should head higher during the week.
+ Gas oil faces resistance at $172.75-$173.50.

IPE Brent crude oil futures are facing a test up at $19 a barrel and then roughly $19.10 but overbought signals suggest the market may find it hard to move far upwards for the time being, technical analysts said on Monday.
September Brent closed one cent firmer on Friday at $18.95 a a barrel and August gas oil was $2.25 a tonne up at $171.50.
"The market's inability to close above $19 was significant," said Nicola Merrell at MMS in London.
"The market is looking overbought at the moment and for the next few sessions it is neutral."

She said a supportive trendline dating from July 21 was currently running through the price action at $18.57. "As long as this area holds then we should move through $19," she said, adding a further level of resistance lay up at Thursday's high of $19.09.
Another support level would be encountered at a previous congestion area of $18.45, she said.
Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS said indicators from the daily, weekly and monthly charts were positive.

September Brent, he said, had broken through a downtrend line dating from May and passing through the highs of July 17. "The odds on upside action shortened following the break of the downtrend line," he said in a weekly report.
"Now we have a quite clear two/three week uptrend line as our potential guide to higher numbers. This very short term dynamic support marker is pivotal in forecasting."
The downtrend line, according to Reuters graphics, lies around $18.35-$18.40 on Monday, while the uptrend line would provide support at around $18.60.
He also said a supportive uptrend line on the monthly chart, dating back to the $12.90 lows in February 1994, remained intact and this lies at around $18.75 a barrel.
Merrell said gas oil faced resistance up at a gap between $172.75 and $173.50.
"The modified stochastics are looking quite overbought but I do not favour a move below $169.50," she said.
